clue.text: This brief message is not allowed to include direction

indicators.note: to include means the phrase for not allowed takes the direction letter inside it

parts.note: not allowed is 'not let', as in not permitted
E is east, a compass direction

explanation.surface: A ban on giving directions in a short communication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to include' puts E inside NOT LET, after the T of NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A short folded card for jotting a quick line to someone is a little note.

clue.text: The goddess of retribution seems in error

indicators.note: in error says the letters of these words are set down wrongly and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone observes that the avenging goddess appears to be mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in error' rearranges SEEMSIN; 'in' looks like part of the indicator but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the deity who punished arrogance and handed out divine vengeance bears this name.

clue.text: A ship's capacity puts a horse in the shade

indicators.note: in, after 'puts a horse', says the horse word goes inside the shade word

parts.note: a shade of colour is a tone
a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: A vessel's size somehow makes a horse look small by comparison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puts a horse in the shade' sounds like outshining it; read literally, NAG goes into TONE.
explanation.definitionFit: The cargo volume or carrying weight of a vessel is measured in tons.

clue.text: Relaxed and turned in because so old

indicators.note: turned says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone eased off and went to bed early because they were so old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points into 'because so old', where ESOOL sits; 'turned' reads that run backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Slack and not tight or tense, as a relaxed grip is.

clue.text: Brown is late possibly to be provoking

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour

indicators.note: possibly says the words is late may appear in another order

explanation.surface: Someone's tardiness may well be a deliberate provocation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges ISLATE into TALISE, which follows TAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To tease by showing something desirable and keeping it out of reach.

clue.text: The serving man found a buyer? That's right

parts.note: goods that found a buyer were sold
i.e. is the Latin abbreviation meaning 'that is'

explanation.surface: A waiter is pleased to confirm he managed to sell something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's right' reads as agreement, but splits into IE (that is) and R (right).
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the army is someone in military service.

clue.text: Criticise wingers

definitions.meaning: to make sly sharp critical remarks

explanation.definitionFit: To carp sniping at someone, and also a wading marsh bird with a long bill.

clue.text: Property-owners making pounds and pounds over ring-roads

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the first pieces above the following ones

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound sterling, from Latin libra
L again stands for pound
O is ring-shaped
RDS is the abbreviation for roads

explanation.surface: Landowners earn money hand over fist from properties beside ring roads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making pounds and pounds' suggests profit, but gives L AND L placed 'over' O and RDS.
explanation.definitionFit: People who let out their buildings to tenants own real estate.

clue.text: Sent in agitated note, being very emotional

indicators.note: agitated says the letters of sent in are stirred into a new order

parts.note: E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A message dispatched in a flustered state, written while very upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitated' rearranges SENTIN to INTENS, and the note E follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling or showing strong passion, deeply felt.

clue.text: Particular esteem

definitions.meaning: a detail or point, as in 'in this regard'

explanation.definitionFit: A detail or aspect, as in 'in every regard', and also high regard for someone.

clue.text: Doctor twelve without point for wind

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the twelve word goes round the point

parts.note: noon is twelve o'clock
S is south, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A doctor tries to blunt a twelve-o'clock gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking: NOON surrounds S.
explanation.definitionFit: A seasonal wind in South Asia, bringing the rainy season.

clue.text: Lights one gets in new building

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: new building says the letters of gets in are put together afresh in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone switches on the lights after entering a newly built block.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new building' rearranges GETSIN into GNITES, which follows I.
explanation.definitionFit: Sets fire to, as a match kindles a flame.

clue.text: Tired fellow coming to a standstill

parts.note: stale means tired, jaded
a mate is a fellow or companion

explanation.surface: An exhausted man grinds to a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock in which neither side can make progress, from the chess position.

clue.text: Clean break or cut

indicators.note: break says the word clean is broken up and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A clean fracture, or just a gash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clean break' reads as a phrase, but 'break' rearranges CLEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce a boil with a blade, a surgical incision.

clue.text: Absolute quiet always required

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: Total silence is constantly demanded.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter or complete, as in pure madness.

clue.text: Stand for certain stuff with much dislike

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric, a particular stuff or cloth
to resent is to dislike strongly

explanation.surface: A protester refuses to tolerate some goods they deeply dislike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuff' is the old word for woven cloth; REP is a corded fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: To act or speak on behalf of, or to symbolise.

clue.text: In the mid winter men think of exequies

definitions.note: plural: funeral rites, where the answer is a single burial

indicators.note: in the mid says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: In deep winter people dwell on funerals.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is wINTERMENThink, across three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Exequies are funeral ceremonies, and a burial is the central rite.

clue.text: Distinctly keen to ditch a social worker

parts.note: a trench is a ditch
an ant is a social insect, and the worker caste does the labour

explanation.surface: Someone is very eager to get rid of a council welfare officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' suggests a welfare job, but is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Incisive and sharp, as cutting criticism is.

clue.text: Date put on some horological creation

indicators.note: put on says the first word is set on, in front of, the next

parts.note: a date is a point in time
a piece is some of something, a portion

explanation.surface: A craftsman sets a date on a clockmaker's creation.
explanation.definitionFit: Horology is the making of clocks, so its product is a clock or watch.

clue.text: Care to add Russian cash to Thai capital?

indicators.note: capital means the first letter of Thai

parts.note: the rouble is the currency of Russia

explanation.surface: Does it worry anyone to pour Russian money into Bangkok?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thai capital' suggests Bangkok, but means its capital letter, T.
explanation.definitionFit: Worry or bother, as in taking pains over something.

clue.text: He meant to change to gas

indicators.note: to change says the letters of he meant must alter their order

explanation.surface: A man intended to switch to gas heating.
explanation.definitionFit: Marsh gas, the chief part of natural gas.

clue.text: What a film is all about

definitions.text: What a film is all about

parts.words: What a film is all about
parts.note: asks literally what a roll of film is wound around, not its plot

explanation.definitionFit: A reel round which camera film or thread is wound.

clue.text: View one example of what the expert knows about Greek letter!

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the second

parts.words: one example of what the expert knows
parts.note: an expert 'knows their onions', a British idiom for being knowledgeable, so an onion is one of them
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A view on what specialists know about the Greek alphabet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to know your onions' is a British idiom for knowing a subject well; ONION goes round PI.
explanation.definitionFit: A belief or judgment held on some matter.

clue.text: More frivolous, though not so colourful

explanation.definitionFit: Less weighty in tone, and also paler in hue.

clue.text: Bizarre route to ruin

indicators.note: to ruin says the word route is wrecked and its letters shuffled

explanation.surface: A strange path leading to destruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Unconventional and eccentric, a French borrowing.

clue.text: Making further use of troops-using manpower

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of troops
pedalling a bike is powering it by human effort

explanation.surface: An army deploying its personnel again.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: Reprocessing waste so it can serve again.

clue.text: Up and down, round and round it goes

indicators.note: up and down says the letters read the same either way along the column

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A thing spinning endlessly up and down.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the word reads the same from top or bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: The spinning part of a machine, like a helicopter's blades.

clue.text: Get Burlington House a good oil-supplier

parts.note: to cop is slang for to get or catch
the Royal Academy, RA, is housed at Burlington House in London

explanation.surface: Someone acquires a fine oil painting for the Royal Academy's home.
explanation.walkthrough: Burlington House on Piccadilly is home to the Royal Academy of Arts; 'oil' suggests paintings.
explanation.definitionFit: Dried coconut kernel, pressed to yield coconut oil.

clue.text: Underwear for the most daring

parts.note: a bra is an undergarment
a vest is a British undergarment for the upper body

explanation.surface: Lingerie for the boldest dresser.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a vest is a sleeveless undershirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of courageous: most fearless.

clue.text: Assign a parking period

parts.note: P is the sign for parking
a point is a full stop, a period

explanation.surface: Allocate a time slot for parking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'period' suggests time, but means the full stop.
explanation.definitionFit: To nominate someone to a job or role.

clue.text: Individual crossing for choice

parts.note: a person marking an X on a ballot paper to pick a candidate

explanation.definitionFit: A voter, someone entitled to choose in a poll.

clue.text: A coach for the retinue escorting royalty

indicators.note: escorting means the retinue goes along beside royalty, so it comes first

parts.note: a train is a retinue of attendants
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A carriage for the courtiers accompanying the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' suggests a carriage, but is a sports instructor; ER = Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who instructs athletes is a sports instructor.
